span.label: mechanisms
span.term: Sounds change the animal's internal state, which simultaneously drives uninstructed body movements and a widespread low-dimensional modulation of cortical (and hippocampal) activity; the apparent multisensory response is that state signal, not an auditory input.
span.note: Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: mechanisms
span.term: Sound-evoked V1 activity is generated by sound-triggered changes in internal and behavioral state rather than by auditory-cortical projections.
span.note: Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: sounds elicit small uninstructed movements, mainly whisker twitches, which are stereotyped across trials and mice and different for each sound
span.note: Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: and the movement precedes the neural activity by a few tens of milliseconds, even with no stimulus present
span.note: Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: the subspace of activity predictable from movement during spontaneous behavior overlaps the sound-related subspace far more than the video-related one
span.note: Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: and the paper stops short of a direct cause - cortical activity and body movements may both arise from changes in the internal state instead
span.note: Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: The results do not rule out genuine auditory signals reaching visual cortex from auditory cortex.
span.note: what this limits: the negative conclusion about auditory input: OUR FINDINGS DO NOT EXCLUDE THE POSSIBILITY OF GENUINE AUDITORY SIGNALS INHERITED BY VISUAL CORTEX FROM AUDITORY CORTEX
Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: Recordings sampled mainly deep layers, not layer 2/3 where earlier conflicting results were obtained.
span.note: what this limits: any comparison with the earlier conflicting layer 2/3 results: OUR V1 RECORDINGS WERE BIASED TOWARD LAYERS 4-6
Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: Auditory projections might affect only a small or low-firing subset of V1 neurons that these recordings missed.
span.note: what this limits: the same negative conclusion, from the sampling side: IT IS ALSO POSSIBLE THAT AUDITORY PROJECTIONS AFFECT ONLY A MINOR FRACTION OF V1 NEURONS, OR THAT THEY AFFECT NEURONS THAT DO NOT FIRE AT HIGH RATES, AND THAT WE MISSED THESE NEURONS IN OUR RECORDINGS
Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: Only facial movements were measured and only with linear analyses; other body parts or richer models could predict the neural activity better.
span.note: what this limits: the claim that facial movement predicts the activity well: IT IS POSSIBLE THAT MOVEMENTS OF OTHER BODY PARTS, OR MORE COMPLEX ANALYSES, WOULD PROVIDE EVEN BETTER PREDICTIONS OF THE NEURAL ACTIVITY ELICITED BY SOUNDS
Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: The behavioral-origin conclusion is scoped to these experiments.
span.note: what this limits: the behavioural-origin conclusion, bounded by the paper itself: THESE RESULTS SUGGEST THAT, AT LEAST IN OUR EXPERIMENTS, THE SOUND-EVOKED ACTIVITY HAD A BEHAVIORAL ORIGIN
Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: genuine auditory signals are not excluded - the projections exist and may carry them for other stimuli or contexts, or affect neurons the recordings missed
span.note: what this limits: the same scope as item 0, with the anatomy: PROJECTIONS FROM AUDITORY TO VISUAL CORTEX EXIST AND MAY CARRY AUDITORY SIGNALS FOR OTHER stimuli or contexts

span.label: movement → neural activity
span.note: CORRELATION WITH A STATED LEAD-LAG, and no type for it. Auditory PC1 activity correlated with movement during spontaneous behaviour (r = 0.29 +/- 0.03 s.e.), and movement PRECEDED neural activity by a few tens of milliseconds. Recording this as `causes` in either direction overstates it; recording it as nothing loses a measured result with its direction. Replaces the retracted concept_edges[32], which pointed the other way.
Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: internal state → behavior
span.note: CO-ORDINATE, NOT CAUSAL. The paper names them as a pair every time - 'low-dimensional changes in internal state and behavior', 'behavioral and state signals have profound effects on sensory areas', 'these behavioral and state signals are low-dimensional and largely orthogonal'. Both are offered as joint explanations of the multisensory signals, and movement is an instance of the behavioural half. No edge type can record that two things occupy the same role.
Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: body movements → multisensory
span.note: THE PAPER'S ACTUAL CLAIM, WHICH THE RETRACTED EDGE INVERTED: stereotyped body movements are elicited by sounds, images and odours, and those movements EXPLAIN neural activity previously interpreted as multisensory. In their own experiments video-evoked responses in hippocampal formation 'could be largely explained by video-evoked body movements'.
Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: sound-evoked activity → hippocampal formation
span.note: THE ACTIVITY RESEMBLES, NOT THE REGIONS: sound-evoked activity in V1 is stereotyped across neurons and mice, independent of auditory-cortex projections, and Quotation withheld - which receives little direct auditory input. The paper's account is that both reflect small stereotyped body movements, so the resemblance is evidence of a COMMON CAUSE and not of any identity between V1 and the hippocampal formation.
Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: AN APPARENTLY MULTISENSORY SIGNAL EXPLAINED AWAY BY behavior: neural activity that is apparently multisensory MAY SIMPLY ARISE from low-dimensional signals associated with internal state and behavior
span.note: Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: and the account being replaced is stated first, with its evidence - suppression by inhibiting auditory cortex, mimicry by stimulating auditory fibers
span.note: Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: THE HYPOTHESIS IS TURNED INTO FOUR ADVANCE PREDICTIONS: low dimension, a broad footprint beyond the cortex, independence from auditory input, and predictability from behavior
span.note: Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: THREE MODELS, AND THE RANKING IS THE FINDING: one from sound identity alone, one from movement alone, one from both - and the behavioral model performs JUST AS WELL as the full model
span.note: Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: with the auditory model's built-in advantage disclosed - it is equivalent to a test-retest prediction and would fit perfectly with infinite trials, so it performs well REGARDLESS of the origin of the activity
span.note: Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: THE MANIPULATION WAS CHOSEN FOR WHAT IT DOES NOT DISTURB: silencing or stimulating auditory cortex would interfere with auditory processing and could affect the sound-evoked behavior, so the fibres were cut instead

span.label: and the control is INSIDE the animal - bilateral recording, the uncut side, the same mouse and the same behavior

span.label: THREE METHOD DIFFERENCES ENUMERATED WHERE THE RESULT CONTRADICTS THE STUDY THAT INTRODUCED THE SAME CUT: intracellular in layers 2/3 against extracellular in layers 4-6, hours against days after surgery, and anesthetized against awake

span.label: AND A THRESHOLD AGAINST A FRACTION: the earlier whisking study used a hard threshold to call a response auditory or movement-related, where this one estimated the fraction explained

span.label: with a between-animal correlation reported against its own within-animal ceiling - 0.34 across mice against a test-retest of 0.44 within them

span.label: A WHOLE LITERATURE'S CONTROLS DECLARED INADEQUATE: distinguishing auditory signals from state and behavior requires careful and systematic controls, WHICH ARE RARELY PERFORMED in passively listening mice

span.label: and the correlation is not claimed as causation - cortical activity and body movements may BOTH arise from changes in the internal state

span.label: RETRACTED (TWO DIFFERENT BRAIN STRUCTURES, DECLARED THE SAME, ON THE STRENGTH OF A RESEMBLANCE BETWEEN THEIR ACTIVITY) · hippocampal formation —same-as→ V1
span.note: RETRACTED: TWO DIFFERENT BRAIN STRUCTURES, DECLARED THE SAME, ON THE STRENGTH OF A RESEMBLANCE BETWEEN THEIR ACTIVITY. The edge is `hippocampal formation --same-as--> V1`. The span: the sound-evoked activity in V1 'is independent of projections from auditory cortex and Quotation withheld, which receives little direct auditory input.' THE SPAN STATES A RESULT ABOUT A PROPERTY AND THE EDGE ASSERTS AN IDENTITY OF THE THINGS. That is `contradicts-needs-differs-in` in mirror image: there an edge asserting disagreement dropped the parameter the disagreement turns on; here an edge asserting agreement drops the property the agreement holds for. The resemblance is between two ACTIVITY PATTERNS and the edge places it between the two REGIONS - and this paper's whole argument is that the shared pattern comes from body movement rather than from either region's sensory input, so the regions being distinct is the point. WHAT THE SPAN DOES SAY (Q-309): housed below. — strength of the relation: 1 — and the signal is the same in a region that receives little direct auditory input, which is the first thing an auditory account cannot hold
Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: RETRACTED (THE INTRODUCTION'S SUMMARY OF A LITERATURE THIS PAPER GOES ON TO OVERTURN) · sound —causes→ neuron
span.note: RETRACTED: THE INTRODUCTION'S SUMMARY OF A LITERATURE THIS PAPER GOES ON TO OVERTURN. The span: 'MANY STUDIES SUGGEST that all cortical sensory areas ... are multisensory. For instance, mouse's primary visual cortex (V1) is influenced by sounds. SOUNDS MAY PROVIDE V1 with global inhibition, modify the neurons' tuning, boost detecti[on]' - five citations in three sentences. AND THIS PAPER'S OWN CONCLUSION IS THAT THE EFFECT IS BODY MOVEMENT: 'neural activity that is apparently multisensory may simply arise from low-dimensional signals associated with internal state and behavior'. The edge records the position the paper argues against. A reader joining on `X --causes--> Y` takes it as a causal relation this paper reports. Q-394. — status: the paper's own words: may · strength of the relation: 1
Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: RETRACTED (CO-ORDINATE CATEGORIES TAGGED AS CAUSE AND EFFECT) · internal state —causes→ movement
span.note: RETRACTED: CO-ORDINATE CATEGORIES TAGGED AS CAUSE AND EFFECT. The edge is `internal state --causes--> movement`. Throughout the span the two are named as a PAIR, never as a chain: 'a possible alternative explanation ... Quotation withheld'; 'BEHAVIORAL AND STATE SIGNALS have profound effects on sensory areas'; 'THESE BEHAVIORAL AND STATE SIGNALS are low-dimensional and largely orthogonal to the high-dimensional code that V1 uses'. Both are offered as joint explanations of the same thing - the multisensory signals - and movement (running, pupil dilation, whisking) is given as an INSTANCE of the behavioural half, not as something internal state produces. The paper's own grammar coordinates them with `and` every time it names them. WHAT THE SPAN DOES SAY (Q-309): housed below as the sibling structure. This is the same family as Kumar2016[7] - two things that share a role tagged as one causing the other - and no edge type can say 'these are co-ordinate'. — strength of the relation: 0.8

span.label: RETRACTED (RELATIONAL SPAN, AND THE ORDER IT STATES RUNS THE OTHER WAY) · spontaneous —causes→ movement
span.note: RETRACTED: RELATIONAL SPAN, AND THE ORDER IT STATES RUNS THE OTHER WAY. The sentence asserts a correlation - 'Quotation withheld (r = 0.29 +/- 0.03)' - and the next clause gives the only temporal evidence in the span: 'MOVEMENT PRECEDED NEURAL ACTIVITY by a few tens of milliseconds'. So the span supports neither the type (`causes` over a correlation) nor the direction (if it licenses an order at all, it is movement -> activity). WHAT THE SPAN DOES SAY (Q-309): a correlation with a measured coefficient and a stated lead-lag, recorded as an unhoused row - schema 0.3 has no relational type, which is the same indexing/proxy gap measured at 8%% of papers. Found by TOOLS/audit_causal_language.py. — strength of the relation: 1 — the coupling survives with no stimulus at all, and the movement PRECEDES the activity by a few tens of milliseconds
